title: Cobb-Douglas production function
plain:
The **Cobb-Douglas** production function multiplies the inputs, each raised to a power:
$$Q = K^aL^b$$
Sometimes there is a constant in front, \(Q = AK^aL^b\) (Herman Miller in Quiz 7 has \(Q = 2K^{0.5}L^{0.5}\)).

Key features:
- Inputs are **imperfect substitutes**: you can trade capital for labor, but the more labor you already have, the more labor it takes to replace one unit of capital. The isoquant is a **convex curve**.
- With an exponent below 1 (like 0.5), each input has **diminishing marginal product**: every extra worker adds less than the one before.
- You need some of both inputs. If either is 0, output is 0.
- The marginal products are on the equation sheet: \(MP_K = aK^{a-1}L^b\) and \(MP_L = bK^aL^{b-1}\). With a constant \(A\) in front, multiply each MP by \(A\).
- The MRTS changes along the isoquant: \(MRTS = \frac{MP_L}{MP_K} = \frac{bK}{aL}\).
why: Cobb-Douglas is the professor's main production function for calculations. The Practice Midterm 2 column of the study guide links this objective to six practice exam questions (Q15 to Q20), more than any other S15 objective.
definition: A Cobb-Douglas production function, \(Q = K^aL^b\), assumes some, but not perfect, substitutability between inputs.

formulas.name: With a constant A in front
formulas.note: Not printed on the sheet. A is just a multiplier, so it carries through the derivative.

formulas.name: MRTS for Cobb-Douglas
formulas.note: The sheet has MRTS = MP_L / MP_K. The simplified bK/(aL) comes from the exponent rules.

derivation:
Start with \(Q = K^aL^b\) and treat K as a constant. Power rule on \(L^b\): \(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial L} = K^a \cdot bL^{b-1}\).

MRTS simplification: divide \(bK^aL^{b-1}\) by \(aK^{a-1}L^b\). Same base, subtract exponents: \(K^{a-(a-1)} = K^1\) and \(L^{(b-1)-b} = L^{-1}\). So \(MRTS = \frac{b}{a}\cdot\frac{K}{L}\).

math.title: Exponent rules (S15 slides pp. 36 to 42)
math.body:
- Multiply, same base: add exponents. \(a^x a^y = a^{x+y}\)
- Divide, same base: subtract. \(\frac{a^x}{a^y} = a^{x-y}\)
- Power of a product: \((xy)^a = x^a y^a\)
- Power of a quotient: \(\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)^a = \frac{x^a}{y^a}\)
- Power of a power: multiply. \((a^x)^y = a^{xy}\)
- Zero power: \(x^0 = 1\)
- Negative power is a reciprocal: \(x^{-a} = \frac{1}{x^a}\), so \(L^{-0.5} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{L}}\)
- Fractional power is a root: \(x^{0.5} = \sqrt{x}\), \(x^{0.25} = \sqrt[4]{x}\)

On a calculator: \(16^{0.25}\) is 16, then the \(y^x\) or ^ key, then 0.25. Answer 2.

math.title: Partial derivatives: hold the other input fixed
math.body: With two inputs, \(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial L}\) means: take the derivative with respect to \(L\) and treat \(K\) as an ordinary number. Example: \(Q = K^{0.5}L^{0.5}\). Treat \(K^{0.5}\) like the 5 in \(5L^{0.5}\): $$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial L} = K^{0.5}\cdot 0.5L^{-0.5} = \frac{0.5K^{0.5}}{L^{0.5}}$$

worked.title: With a constant (Comprehension Quiz 7 Q4)
worked.problem: \(Q = 2K^{0.5}L^{0.5}\) with \(K = 9\). Find \(MP_L\) as a function of L.

graph.caption: Cobb-Douglas isoquants (here Q = 2K^0.5 L^0.5) are convex. Slide the point right: the MRTS readout falls.
Short run with K fixed at 9: MP_L falls at every L (diminishing returns everywhere when b < 1).

traps: a goes with K and b goes with L. Mixing them up gives MP_K when you wanted MP_L.
Subtract 1 from the exponent of the input you differentiate, and leave the other input's exponent alone.
If the function has a constant in front (2K^0.5 L^0.5), multiply the MP by it. The sheet formula has no constant.
Cobb-Douglas is imperfect substitution. Perfect substitution is linear; no substitution is Leontief (Reading Quiz Q5).
